physical_cues.cue: The circular stone building you can go inside if it is open

beat_evidence.script_excerpt: This circular stone structure — taller in some earlier incarnations — has been at the center of New York life over the years. In 1807, the West Battery, as it was then called, was built as a fort on a landfill island in the water off Manhat
After 1823 the site became an extremely popular entertainment center called Castle Gardens. The 'Swedish Nightingale,' Jenny Lind, was a headliner here in 1850.

physical_cues.cue: Ellis Island visible from here, to the right of the Statue of Liberty, its main hall topped with four little spires

beat_evidence.script_excerpt: In 1855, the space was transformed once more, into the city's first immigrant processing center. Over eight million new arrivals — a full two-thirds of those who came to the United States at this time — spent their first hours in the countr

The famed architectural team of McKim, Mead, and White then stepped in and transformed the site into the nation's first aquarium, visited by about ninety million people until it was moved in 1941 to Coney Island. After the site stood empty
